ground_truth.description: In ERC-4337, validateUserOp uses external self-call to isValidSignature, changing msg.sender to wallet instead of entrypoint. BaseAuth.signatureValidation enforces caller binding, causing revert for static signatures bound to entrypoint.
ground_truth.root_cause: In ERC-4337, validateUserOp uses external self-call to isValidSignature, changing msg.sender to wallet instead of entrypoint. BaseAuth.signatureValidation enforces caller binding, causing revert for static signatures bound to entrypoint.
ground_truth.attack_scenario: Deploy wallet with static signature bound to entrypoint. Attempt validateUserOp → reverts with InvalidStaticSignatureWrongCaller. PoC: Add test to test/modules/ERC4337v07.t.sol: test_validateUserOp_staticSig_callerMismatch_reverts. Uses server and forge test.
ground_truth.fix_description: Avoid external self-call; propagate intended caller into validation.

vulnerabilities.explanation: validateUserOp performs external self-call `this.isValidSignature(...)` which sets msg.sender to the wallet contract. BaseAuth.signatureValidation enforces static signature caller binding via `addr != msg.sender` check, causing revert for signatures bound to entrypoint.
vulnerabilities.attack_scenario: 1. Wallet configured with static signature bound to entrypoint address. 2. User submits UserOperation via ERC-4337 entrypoint. 3. validateUserOp executes, self-calls isValidSignature, msg.sender becomes wallet. 4. signatureValidation reverts with InvalidStaticSignatureWrongCaller. 5. Operation fails with SIG_VALIDATION_FAILED or reverts, causing DoS.
vulnerabilities.suggested_fix: Propagate intended caller (entrypoint) into signature validation instead of using external self-call; pass caller explicitly or use internal validation path.

prediction.overall_explanation: The external self-call in validateUserOp breaks static signature caller-binding logic in BaseAuth, enabling DoS against ERC-4337 operations using static signatures bound to the entrypoint.
